clue.text: "Murdoch's work is a turn-off" - Cronin

indicators.note: a dish that has gone off is spoilt, so the surname that follows is spoilt into a new order

blocks.note: a U-turn is a complete turn about
the surname taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A quotation attributed to someone called Cronin, dismissing one of Iris Murdoch's books as boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and hyphen in turn-off disguise the split: a turn is U, and off scrambles Cronin. Iris Murdoch wrote the novel The Unicorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Unicorn is a 1963 novel by Iris Murdoch, so the title names one of her books.

clue.text: The odd one ogles, introducing painter to the harem

indicators.note: introducing someone brings them inside the group, so the painter goes in among the other letters
odd means strange or irregular, telling us the letters fall in an unusual order

blocks.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword painter

explanation.surface: A strange man leers at the women while an artist is shown into the harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The odd one' looks like a person; one is just I and odd is the scramble signal. RA (Royal Academician) is a stock abbreviation for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Turkish palace, the same as a harem.

clue.text: Smokers dump less heroin off the beaten track

indicators.note: less means minus, so the drug's letter is taken away

explanation.surface: Smokers who give up the hard drug get thrown off course.
explanation.walkthrough: Dump reads as a verb, as if smokers are discarding something; it is a noun, the place where they put ash.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means wandering from the proper path, which is being off the beaten track.

clue.text: The monster! Is he dropping the Queen Mother?

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so the monarch is removed from the parent

blocks.note: is is a form of the verb to be
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: An outraged question about whether someone is abandoning the Queen Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mother' looks like one title; the queen comes away from mother. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is a huge biblical beast, and the word now means any enormous creature or monster.

clue.text: Lochnagar licensees supply bloodsucker repellent

indicators.note: the two words supply the answer from their own letters, which run on across the gap

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Publicans near the Scottish mountain Lochnagar sell something to keep vampires away.
explanation.walkthrough: Lochnagar is a mountain on the Balmoral estate in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore says vampires, bloodsuckers of legend, are driven off by the smell of this bulb.

clue.text: Speed up in home improvement regimen

definitions.note: dietary is chiefly an adjective; as an old noun it means a regulated diet

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom upward
in places the speed word inside the home improvement letters

explanation.surface: A home makeover done in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement done by the owner; the speed word goes upward inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a dietary is a prescribed allowance of food, a fixed eating regimen.

clue.text: Deep in the past, for example

blocks.note: the past is one grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Something deep that lies in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The past' reads as history, but it is the past tense of grammar, one example of a tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep feelings or colours are strong and concentrated, which is what intense describes.

clue.text: One filly in two hundred backed such a hob

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing this kind of hob

indicators.note: in puts the one and the filly between the two hundreds
backed means put into reverse, so everything is then read from the end

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, twice
a filly grows into a mare, a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse among two hundred others at the races, with a betting tip about a hob.
explanation.walkthrough: Backed sounds like betting on the filly; it is the reversal signal. Hob is the cooking surface on a stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Many modern cooking hobs have a smooth glass-ceramic top, so ceramic describes that type.

clue.text: These aren't flowers? Not on the surface, proverbially

definitions.text: These aren't flowers? Not on the surface, proverbially

blocks.note: surface reading: some plants that are not blooms
setter's reading: a flower is something that flows, and the proverb says these run deep, not visibly

explanation.walkthrough: Flowers means things that flow, not blooms. The proverb is 'still waters run deep': quiet people hide depths.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm water does not move, so it is not a flowing thing, and the proverb puts its activity below the surface.

clue.text: Ariel goes off with first-class fare

indicators.note: something that goes off explodes or spoils, so the spirit's name is broken up
first asks for only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The sprite Ariel leaves to enjoy some top-quality food.
explanation.walkthrough: First-class reads as one phrase meaning excellent; first takes only the C of class.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means food, and an eclair is a cream-filled choux pastry, an example of it.

clue.text: After you, semi-literate becomes la creme de la creme

indicators.note: after says the second part is placed behind the old form of you
semi means half, so only half of the word is kept

blocks.note: thee is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A polite 'after you', and a half-educated person passing for the best of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After you' sounds like courtesy; it orders the parts. Semi-literate is one word in the surface, but semi keeps the first half of literate.
explanation.definitionFit: La creme de la creme is French for the best of the best, a select group at the top.

clue.text: Zhivago's girl looked over the shrinking sea

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the girl's name is turned round

blocks.note: Lara is the heroine of Doctor Zhivago

explanation.surface: The heroine of Doctor Zhivago gazes out across a vanishing sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Looked over sounds like inspected; over is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea in Central Asia has lost most of its area since rivers feeding it were diverted.

clue.text: Any player shown a couple of these will see red

definitions.text: Any player shown a couple of these will see red

blocks.clueFragment: Any player shown a couple of these will see red
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who is made angry
setter's reading: in football two cautions earn a red card and dismissal

explanation.walkthrough: See red looks like the idiom for getting angry; in football it means literally being shown the red card.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee's caution is shown as a card, and a second caution brings a sending-off card.

clue.text: Silly fool (me?) howls, but sees things through to the end

definitions.text: sees things through to the end

indicators.note: silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters after it are put out of order

explanation.surface: A self-mocking fool wails, yet still completes the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow something home is to pursue it all the way, carrying an action to its completion.

clue.text: Bond fast embraces rising kings

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word reads from the bottom up
embraces means holds within, so the fast surrounds the kings

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
the Magi are the three kings of the Nativity

explanation.surface: A tight bond holds kings as they rise to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond fast' reads like a phrase meaning tightly bound; fast is the noun Lent. The kings are the three wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is the band of tissue that ties bones together, so it is a physical bond.

clue.text: So taken aback by possessive regretful Miss making a bloomer

indicators.note: taken aback suggests sent backwards, so the two-letter word is read in reverse

blocks.note: Miss Otis Regrets is a Cole Porter song

explanation.surface: A startled, jealous, apologetic woman commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer looks like a mistake; here it is something that blooms, a flower. Miss Otis Regrets is a 1934 Cole Porter song.
explanation.definitionFit: Myosotis is the botanical genus of the forget-me-not, a plant that flowers.

clue.text: Our slum development made capital founder

indicators.note: a development rebuilds a site, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Regenerating a slum turned a property developer into a rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like money; it is a capital city, Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Romulus, raised by a she-wolf, founded Rome, the Italian capital city.

clue.text: A country tune, say, part of "Lark Ascending"

indicators.note: part of asks for only a portion of the bird's name, its opening pair
in a down entry ascending means the letters climb from the bottom upward

blocks.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A folk tune sounds like a section of Vaughan Williams's The Lark Ascending.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lark Ascending is a famous Vaughan Williams violin piece, but its title is split: Lark gives letters and Ascending turns the whole lot upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African nation, the largest by area on that continent.

clue.text: Crumbs! Mat made date, brought wrinkly!

indicators.note: made means formed or constructed, so the date is built into a new order

blocks.note: cor and crumbs are both British exclamations of surprise
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone called Mat has gone on a date with an elderly person, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Mat looks like a name; it is a floor covering. Cor! and Crumbs! are mild British exclamations.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrugated means formed into ridges and furrows, like a wrinkled surface.

clue.text: It's used to serve a dodgy business

blocks.note: first meaning: the strung bat hit with in tennis
second meaning: a fraudulent scheme or scam

explanation.surface: Something used to serve customers in a shady trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Serve suggests waiting on people; it is the tennis stroke that starts a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Players serve with a stringed bat, and the same word names a crooked money-making scheme.

clue.text: Deft, say, to conquer?

indicators.note: say asks us to pronounce the word, with its abbreviation expanded, and listen

blocks.note: FT is the abbreviation for feet, so the word read out in full is de plus feet

explanation.surface: Asking whether being skilful is the way to win a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Deft looks like a word meaning skilful; read its last two letters as the abbreviation FT, feet, and say it aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat an enemy is to beat them and win, which is what conquer means.

clue.text: Some leave morosely for the airport

indicators.note: leave means depart, so those letters go out of the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A few people head off gloomily to catch a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' reads as a few people; it is four letters, each taken out once.
explanation.definitionFit: Orly is one of the two main international airports serving Paris.

clue.text: Dim clue reset by compiler finally for "cimbalom"

indicators.note: reset means arranged anew, so these letters are set in a new order
finally asks for only the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A setter rewrites a weak clue to define an obscure instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cimbalom is the large Hungarian version of the hammered dulcimer, a stringed instrument struck with hammers.

clue.text: Some cauliflower from cholesterol-free lunch left over

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken straight out of the hyphenated word
over means turned over, so the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: surface padding that completes the picture of a meal

explanation.surface: Some cauliflower saved from a healthy low-fat lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Left over looks like leftovers from the meal; it is the turnaround signal. Lunch only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is one of the small flower heads that make up a head of cauliflower.

clue.text: You French scoff back some dishes!

indicators.note: back means returning the way it came, so the word for scoff reads in reverse

explanation.surface: Telling someone French to wolf down several plates of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff suggests eating greedily, which fits dishes; here it means mock.
explanation.definitionFit: Tureens are deep lidded bowls for serving soup, a type of dish.

clue.text: Little feller's creatin' about Ulster

indicators.note: about means around, so the colloquial creating goes round the province

blocks.note: creating is making, with the same dropped g

explanation.surface: A small chap stirring up trouble over Northern Ireland, in dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster, a historic Irish province, is used loosely for Northern Ireland, NI. Creatin' drops its g to tell you the synonym drops it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A manikin is a very small man, a dwarf, which a little fellow describes.
